html:
SMTO-EXE-0051 — No one is signed in at the computer's screen for SMTO to use

GUID: ded642ef-6f27-5cbd-8a56-5efa1a28a4ae
Slug: desktop-no-session
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: desktop

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't find a signed-in desktop on the Gateway computer, so it can't see or work with the windows and apps there. Nothing on that computer was changed.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Sign in at the Gateway computer's screen and leave the session open and unlocked. Working with windows and apps needs a live desktop to act in.
  2. Start the Gateway (SMTO's helper program on that computer) from inside that desktop, as the signed-in user, not as a background service or over a text-only remote connection. A Gateway started outside the desktop can't see its windows, even when someone is signed in.
  3. Open Settings › Setup › Gateways, select Check connection for that Gateway, then ask SMTO again. This refreshes what SMTO knows the Gateway can do now that a desktop is available.

What success looks like

  • SMTO can list the open windows on that computer without this error.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages that Gateway computer, mentioning whether it runs Windows, macOS or Linux.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Gateway's Desktop backend found no usable interactive session (for example no X11 DISPLAY, a non-console macOS session, Windows session 0, or a headless adapter without window support).

What this means

  • Desktop readiness or native window access could not establish the required interactive session, including a missing X11 DISPLAY or an adapter without window-session support. These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.

Why this can happen

  • Desktop readiness or native window access could not establish the required interactive session, including a missing X11 DISPLAY or an adapter without window-session support.

How to diagnose it

  • Check desktop.summary and the Gateway account's interactive session on the intended host.

How to fix it

  • Log in to the selected Gateway host's desktop and run the Gateway inside that session as the same user: on Linux, an X11 session with DISPLAY set; on macOS, the console session; on Windows, an interactive (non-zero) session with an input desktop. Then refresh the Gateway's capabilities and confirm desktop.summary reports interactive_session=true and windows can be listed.
  • Log in to the selected Gateway desktop and run the Gateway in that session.

Retry and execution caution

  • Log in to the selected Gateway desktop and run the Gateway in that session.

How to verify the fix

  • The same Gateway reports a usable interactive desktop and can list its windows.

What not to do

  • Do not bypass identity protection or automatically replay an uncertain mutation.

Technical notes

  • These operations address the selected Gateway desktop. Metadata discovery does not authorize content reads, and a native control request is not proof of completed effects; retain exact operation and target identities.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
